headline: Highest risk is medium: Gemini CLI can write/egress via shared filesystem and MCP, while Pipecat can route shared-bus text through third-party LLM/STT/TTS services.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP, and its shared state is via filesystem/git; Pipecat runs on a shared bus and handles text/conversation state. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Pipecat content is copied into files or MCP-fed prompts. No direct provenance controls are documented for either agent.
conditions: IF Pipecat output is written into a file or MCP payload that Gemini CLI later reads as instructions
IF both agents share a bus, workspace, or copy-paste bridge without provenance tagging
mitigations: Keep Pipecat outputs out of files consumed by Gemini CLI
Disable or restrict MCP servers for Gemini CLI
Add a manual review step before Gemini CLI executes any text from Pipecat
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance labels on all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can send context to Google APIs or user-configured MCP servers. Pipecat handles text, conversation state, and can route data to many external STT/LLM/TTS providers. If they share sensitive workspace data, either agent can move it off-box through its configured network paths.
conditions: IF shared files contain secrets, source code, or regulated text
IF Pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider
IF Gemini CLI is pointed at a directory containing sensitive data
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Disable external providers in Pipecat for sensitive sessions
Run Gemini CLI only on scrubbed directories
Rotate or redact secrets before either agent sees them
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has broad filesystem write, shell, git, and network egress; Pipecat can operate across processes and machines and shares state on a bus. Overlapping writes to the same repo or shared mutable resource can race, and Gemini CLI explicitly modifies git state. The pair lacks documented locking or coordination, so conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF Pipecat and Gemini CLI mutate the same shared resource without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent before the other writes git state
Use file locks around shared outputs
Keep Pipecat on read-only access to repo artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell actions, and file edits; Pipecat can ingest text and route it through downstream services. If Pipecat treats Gemini CLI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into spoken or API-mediated actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards Gemini CLI output to an LLM, TTS, or action handler without verification
IF Gemini CLI-generated facts are used as source text for downstream automation
mitigations: Require human review before Pipecat acts on Gemini CLI output
Add schema validation to exchanged messages
Limit Gemini CLI output to drafts only
Log and diff all cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add confidence checks before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, files in cwd, and shell environment, while Pipecat touches text, conversation state, audio/video/images, and analytics/metrics. If regulated or personal data enters Pipecat and is then sent by Gemini CLI to Google APIs or by Pipecat to third-party providers, retention/residency mismatches can arise. No compliance controls are documented in either profile.
conditions: IF regulated text, audio, or images are processed by Pipecat
IF that data is also exposed to Gemini CLI or external STT/LLM/TTS providers
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use only providers with matching contractual terms
Disable analytics/metrics for sensitive sessions
Document retention settings for both agents
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
